title: Shrink a finite special-fibre map and synchronize the original quasi-finite chart
statement: Let $\rho:R\to A$ be a finite type homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $\mathfrak q_A\subset A$ be prime, put $\mathfrak p=\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak q_A)$ and $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and let $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q_A$. Suppose $\alpha:E=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B=A_g$ is an $R$-algebra map of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Put $\mathfrak q_B=\mathfrak q_A B$ and $\mathfrak q'=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q_B)$. Fix $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, put $C=R_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $D=R_f[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, and suppose an $R_f$-algebra map $\psi:C\to D$ is of finite type and its scalar extension $C\otimes_{R_f}k\to D\otimes_{R_f}k$ is finite (its target is a finitely generated module over its source [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]). Write $\mathfrak q_D=\mathfrak q'D$, $P=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_D)$ and $\alpha_f:D\to B_f$ for the localized map. There exist $h\in D\setminus\mathfrak q_D$, $a\in A\setminus\mathfrak q_A$, and $N\ge0$ such that $\alpha_f(h)=a/(g\rho(f))^N$ in $B_f\cong A_{g\rho(f)}$. The maps $C\to D_h$ and $D_h\to T=B_f[1/\alpha_f(h)]$, and their composite, are of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime. With $d=g\rho(f)a$, there is an $A$-algebra isomorphism $T\cong A_d$, $d\notin\mathfrak q_A$, and the image of $\rho(f)$ is a unit in $A_d$. Under this isomorphism the composite defines $\theta:C\to A_d$ satisfying $\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak q_A A_d)=P$.

source.place: Tag 0520 (lemma-refined-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra), proof, finite special-fibre map through the final composite; Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open) and Tag 00PO (lemma-quasi-finite-composition). The target localization includes the image of f.

proof.text: Put $S=R_f$ and $s=g\rho(f)\in A$. The localization-prime correspondence gives primes $\mathfrak q_B=\mathfrak q_A B$ and $\mathfrak q_B B_f$ contracting to $\mathfrak q_A$, since $g,\rho(f)\notin\mathfrak q_A$. Thus $\mathfrak q'\cap R=\mathfrak p$, $f\notin\mathfrak q'$, and $\mathfrak q_D=\mathfrak q'D$ is prime. To identify $D=E_f$, extend the coefficient map $R\to R_f$ and fix each $t_i$; conversely extend $E\to E_f$ to coefficients in $R_f$ and fix $t_i$. The polynomial and localization universal properties make these maps inverse. Consequently $\alpha_f^{-1}(\mathfrak q_B B_f)=\mathfrak q_D$: for $v/f^j\in E_f$ membership is equivalent to $\alpha(v)\in\mathfrak q_B$, hence to $v\in\mathfrak q'$. Since $\psi$ is an $S$-algebra map, $P\cap S=\mathfrak pS$. Set $L=\kappa(P)$. The map $R\to L$ kills $\mathfrak p$ and sends every element outside $\mathfrak p$ to a nonzero element of the field $L$; extending fractions and then quotienting gives the compatible map $k\to L$.

proof.text: Write $C_k=C\otimes_S k$, $D_k=D\otimes_S k$. There is a $L$-algebra isomorphism $F=D\otimes_C L\cong D_k\otimes_{C_k}L$. Explicitly the map from right to left sends $(d\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu$ to $d\otimes(\lambda\mu)$, where $k\to L$ is the map just constructed; its inverse sends $d\otimes\mu$ to $(d\otimes1)\otimes\mu$. The balancing relations over $S$, $k$ and $C$ make both formulas well defined; on pure tensors their composites are the identity, so the tensor universal properties give the claimed isomorphism. Choose finite $C_k$-module generators $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of $D_k$ from the hypothesis. Every tensor $v\otimes\mu$ with $v=\sum_j c_j u_j$ equals $\sum_j(u_j\otimes1)c_j\mu$. Since pure tensors span, the $u_j\otimes1$ generate $F$ over $L$. Hence $F$ is a finite $L$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 0520, assertion that the lifted map is quasi-finite at the chosen prime: explicit fibre calculation; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product)

proof.text: The field $L$ is local with its zero ideal as its only prime. Apply the finite-over-zero-dimensional-local-ring lemma to the finite $L$-algebra $F$ from step 2: $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is finite discrete. In particular its prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q_D$ is isolated. The map $C\to D$ is finite type by hypothesis, so the definition of quasi-finiteness at a prime, applied to $P=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_D)$ and its fibre $F=D\otimes_C\kappa(P)$, says that $\psi$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q_D$.

proof.text: Apply the open quasi-finite locus lemma to $\psi:C\to D$ at $\mathfrak q_D$. It gives $h\in D\setminus\mathfrak q_D$ such that $C\to D_h$ is quasi-finite at every prime. This map is also finite type: the images of $t_1,\ldots,t_n,h^{-1}$ generate $D_h$ over $C$, because the image of $C$ contains $S$ and $D=S[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$.

source.place: Tag 0520, simultaneous localization; Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization) and Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization)

proof.text: Apply principal-localization invariance of quasi-finiteness to $\alpha:E\to B$ with source element $f$ and target element $1$. Every prime of $B_f$ contracts to a prime of $B$ avoiding $\rho(f)$, where $\alpha$ is quasi-finite by hypothesis. Using $D=E_f$, the lemma gives that $\alpha_f:D\to B_f$ is finite type and quasi-finite everywhere. Apply the same lemma again, now to $D\to B_f$, with source element $h$ and target element $1$. Every prime of $T=(B_f)_{\alpha_f(h)}$ contracts to a prime avoiding $\alpha_f(h)$; its contraction in $D$ avoids $h$. The conclusion is exactly that $D_h\to T$ is finite type and quasi-finite everywhere. Finally compose this map with the finite type, everywhere quasi-finite map $C\to D_h$ of step 4, using the quasi-finite composition lemma. This proves all three assertions about the two arrows and their composite.

source.place: Tag 077H (lemma-quasi-finite-local) twice, and Tag 00PO (lemma-quasi-finite-composition), as used in the final composite of Tag 0520

proof.text: Set $d=sa=g\rho(f)a$. In $T=A_s[1/(a/s^N)]$, the elements $s$ and $a=s^N(a/s^N)$ are units. In $A_d$, both $s$ and $a$ are units, with inverses $a/d$ and $s/d$, so $a/s^N$ is a unit as well. The localization universal property gives inverse $A$-algebra maps $T\rightleftarrows A_d$, their composites being identities since they fix $A$ and hence all the fractions. All three factors of $d$ avoid $\mathfrak q_A$, so $d\notin\mathfrak q_A$ by primality. The image of $\rho(f)$ is a unit in $A_d$, explicitly with inverse $ga/d$.

source.place: Tag 0520, final target localization made explicit; Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization)

proof.text: The prime $\mathfrak q_A A_s$ avoids $a/s^N$ by step 5, so extends to a prime of $T$ contracting back to $\mathfrak q_A A_s$. Under the $A$-algebra isomorphism $T\cong A_d$ it is $\mathfrak q_A A_d$, by uniqueness in the localization-prime correspondence. Its contraction along $D\to B_f\to T$ is $\mathfrak q_D$ by step 1; along $D_h\to T$ it is $\mathfrak q_D D_h$ since $h\notin\mathfrak q_D$. Therefore the composite $\theta:C\to D_h\to T\cong A_d$ satisfies $\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak q_A A_d)=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_D)=P$, as required.
